metadata.notes: Chapter contains two scenes in the same month: inspection of colony ship construction, then an all-Bobs strategy meeting in Earth orbit.

believes: Earth's climate is continuing to deteriorate and may be accelerating.
Current shipbuilding capacity will not be enough to evacuate all fifteen million remaining humans from Sol in time.
Diverting major resources to alternate survival schemes would delay colony-ship construction too much to improve overall survival odds.

scenes.summary: Riker inspects the half-built colony ships and reviews the manufacturing and raw-material situation supporting their construction.
Riker, Homer, Charles, and Arthur meet in Earth orbit to discuss worsening climate conditions and possible alternatives to the current evacuation plan.

quotes.speaker: Arthur
quotes.text: And the worst part is that even if we stick to the plan as is, we probably can’t save everyone.
quotes.context: Arthur sums up the grim conclusion of the Sol Bobs' strategy meeting about evacuation limits.

events.text: Riker's Sol shipbuilding program reaches the stage where two large colony ships are half-built and a third is projected four months behind them.

The Sol Bobs conclude that current evacuation efforts are unlikely to save all fifteen million remaining humans, and no alternative scheme they discuss improves the overall outlook without delaying shipbuilding.

summary.one_line: Riker reviews steady colony-ship progress in Sol, then confronts with the other Bobs the grim likelihood that evacuation capacity will still fall short of saving everyone.
summary.paragraph: Riker inspects the two half-built colony ships and notes that construction is proceeding well, with manufacturing and raw-material supply currently keeping pace. Homer’s Earth-salvage operation has become productive enough to return printers to regular ship production, but the larger math remains brutal: there may be enough material for many more ships eventually, just not soon enough. In an all-Bobs meeting with Homer, Charles, and Arthur, they brainstorm alternatives like relocation within Earth, orbital habitats, moon colonies, and giant space mirrors. Every option either fails to address the real survival constraints or would delay shipbuilding so badly that it makes the situation worse. Riker ends the chapter facing the painful reality that even staying on plan may not save everyone.
events: Riker inspects the partially completed colony ships and confirms that construction, parts production, and raw-material supply are all currently on track.
He reflects on the continuing political pressure over evacuation priorities and the unresolved problem of the fifteen million people still stranded on Earth.
Riker reviews Homer’s salvage work lifting metal from Earth, which has improved supply but not enough to solve the timetable problem.
Homer, Charles, Arthur, and Riker meet in Earth orbit and openly acknowledge that they are unlikely to evacuate everyone out-system.
They consider triage, internal relocation, space mirrors, space stations, and moon colonies, but reject each idea as too slow, too costly, or too disruptive to shipbuilding.
The meeting ends on a bleak note as the Bobs admit they may have no better option than to continue the current plan and hope it is enough.
summary.pov_emotional_arc: Riker moves from practical satisfaction at visible engineering progress to weary despair as he confronts the limits of what that progress can actually save.

open_threads.text: Bob now knows replicants can go insane during unstructured subjective time, raising the question of whether he can stay sane through training and standby.
Bob is denied access to genealogy records and remains cut off from any living descendants or family connections.
Bob learns that hostile factions inside FAITH could sabotage or terminate the replicant project.
Bob now knows several rival nations are racing to launch interstellar probes, with the Brazilian Empire suspected of sabotage and armed competition.
Bob learns the FAITH facility has a hidden tactical nuclear failsafe that could kill him and everyone nearby if someone decides he is too dangerous.
Minister Jacoby leaves after threatening Dr. Landers, raising the question of whether he will act against the replicant project.
The launch turns into a confused orbital battle with missiles, military ships, and multiple unknown attackers, leaving the identity of the factions involved unresolved.
After disabling his endocrine control system, Bob begins fully mourning his lost human life, raising the question of how this emotional release will affect him going forward.
Bob concludes that at least one more Brazilian Empire ship exists and that USE, Chinese, and possibly Australian probes may also be active somewhere in space.
Bob's first cohort of clones diverges in personality immediately, raising questions about how future Bob society and identity will evolve.
Milo has found two apparently habitable living worlds at Omicron Eridani, but it remains unresolved whether Earth life and humans are biologically compatible with them.
Milo departs for 82 Eridani, opening the question of what he will find there.
Bill and Garfield now have a working subspace communications system, raising the question of how quickly they can deploy it across multiple star systems.
Riker and Colonel Butterworth agree to try building colony ships in Sol, raising the question of whether the surviving humans can endure long enough to launch them and where they will go.
Bob has discovered intelligent fire-using natives on Delta Eridani 4, raising the question of whether and how he will make first contact.
One Brazilian vessel escapes the destruction of the Alpha Centauri construction yard, leaving its destination and future threat unresolved.
Calvin and Goku conclude Alpha Centauri should be reinforced with combat-class Bobs, raising the question of whether Bill will approve and send them.
Bob has identified an unusually inventive Deltan boy named Archimedes, raising the question of how far his intelligence and toolmaking will develop.
Riker reprioritizes transport-vessel construction for refugee movement, raising the question of how much this will delay colony-ship production.
Riker has convened a global survivor assembly, but it remains unresolved whether the enclaves can create workable governance and cooperate on evacuation and survival priorities.
The Deltans remain under ongoing predation pressure from gorilloids, raising the question of whether Bob's indirect aid and planned drone defenses will be enough to secure their survival.
VEHEMENT is escalating anonymous threats and opportunistic violence in Sol, raising the question of whether it will disrupt evacuation and governance efforts.
Riker has discovered living descendants of Andrea Johansson, raising the question of how this new family connection will affect his decisions and emotional life.
Luke has departed for Kappa Ceti, opening the question of what he will find there.
Bender has departed for Gamma Leporis A, opening the question of what he will find there.
Bob now has the ability and willingness to speak directly to the Deltans through a modified drone, raising the question of how far he will go in overt intervention.
Linus has rescued the unstable Australian replicant Henry Roberts and begun VR-based rehabilitation, leaving open whether Henry can fully recover and function again.
Epsilon Indi appears sparse and only partly surveyed, leaving open whether Linus will find anything in the system worth long-term development or colonization.

recent_events.text: Bob sends Luke and Bender out to new stars and prepares to speak directly to the Deltans for the first time.
Linus reaches Epsilon Indi, finds a broken Australian replicant named Henry Roberts, and begins trying to save his mind.
Riker gets Bill's SCUT working in Sol and uses the breakthrough to unveil Vulcan and Romulus as humanity's immediate evacuation targets.
Bill gets a promising new terraforming tool for Ragnarök and is forced to rethink how he works with Garfield.
